source.name: BBC World News RSS
source.title: Mistrial declared in Lindsay Clancy murder case, after jury deadlocks
source.summary: The mistrial now puts the murder case - and Clancy's future - in limbo as to whether she will be held criminally liable in the deaths of her three kids.
source.evidence_text:
A judge in Massachusetts ended Lindsay Clancy’s murder trial with a mistrial after the jury remained unable to agree.
The case concerns the deaths of Clancy’s three children.
Jurors had considered the case for a week after hearing weeks of testimony.
A further court hearing was scheduled for later in the month to address what happens next.
Clancy’s lawyer unsuccessfully tried to stop the judge from declaring a mistrial.
The prosecutor said the legal team would discuss whether to pursue another trial; no decision was announced that day.
The report explained that a deadlocked jury had delivered neither a conviction nor a finding of not guilty.
Clancy remained held on the existing charges following the mistrial.
The defence asked the state’s highest court to require continued jury deliberations, but the request was refused.
The report described widespread public attention and disagreement over the case.
